source_text: Ἐπ' ἀμφοτέρων τῶν περὶ τῆς θεότητος καὶ τῆς ἀνθρωπότητος λεγομένων τίθησιν τὸ ἐγώ, ὡς τὴν μὲν διάνοιαν τῶν ῥημάτων ἐκ τῆς ἀκολουθίας φαίνεσθαι, τὴν δὲ
thought_title: The I placed on both natures
orientation: Cyril is explaining how the pronoun “I” in Christ’s saying is used of both his divinity and his humanity.
pass_a_gloss: In the case of both the things said about the divinity and the humanity, he places the I, so that the meaning of the words is shown from the context, and the

choices.why: The preposition ἐπί with genitive here means “in the case of,” indicating the sphere of application for the two sets of statements.
The participle is passive and plural, referring to statements made about each nature; “things said” preserves the passive force.
The verb means to put or set; “places” keeps the concrete sense of positioning the pronoun within the statements.
The glossary requires “I” for ἐγώ, and the article marks it as the pronoun being discussed.
The conjunction introduces a result clause explaining the purpose of placing the I.
The noun refers to the thought or sense of the words; “meaning” is the natural English equivalent.

pass_b_english: Christ uses the pronoun “I” for statements about both his divinity and his humanity, so that the meaning of the words is shown by their context, while the distinction of the natures is shown by the difference in what is said.

last_rejected.quote: while the discernment of the natures is shown by the difference in what is said.
last_rejected.why: Source has δὲ marking contrast; English adds 'discernment' and 'difference in what is said' not in source.
last_rejected.fix: while the distinction of the natures is shown by the difference in what is said.
last_rejected.ruling: τὴν δὲ continues from τὴν μὲν...τὴν δὲ construction; 'discernment' and 'difference' are implied by context and normal rendering of this contrastive pair.
